analysis: What changed vs the 5 AM brief: the tape is roughly flat to slightly steadier — S&P futures -0.9% vs -1.0%, Nasdaq-100 -1.7% vs -1.9% — but the individual givebacks deepened. Nvidia drifted from -5.2% to -6% premarket, HPE from -10.9% to -12%, Semtech from -8.4% to -12%, Dell from -5.4% to -7% ahead of its print. The beat-and-fall pattern is now the morning's dominant theme: HPE, Semtech and (single-source) Analog Devices all fell after strong results, while beat-and-raise names — Best Buy, Agilent, Dick's (+16.7%) — were bought. Fresh items since 5 AM: Sanofi's $41B Insmed acquisition (INSM +15%), an Alibaba subsidiary added to a US chip blacklist, and Anthropic slipping below its $83 IPO price. Rate-futures pricing nudged to a 97.6% chance of a 25bp December hike (Barchart), a touch softer than the 100% hike likelihood carried in the 5 AM brief. Signal vs noise: the deepening guide-driven selloffs, the M&A and blacklist news, and Anthropic under its IPO price are signal; the exact premarket percentages in a thin Thanksgiving-week tape are noise. The next real tests are 10 AM ET consumer confidence, 2 PM ET FOMC minutes, and Dell/HP/Workday after the close.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures point to a lower open, roughly steady vs the 5 AM brief: S&P 500 futures -0.9%, Nasdaq-100 futures -1.7%, Dow futures -0.4% in the latest Investopedia prints (WSJ live coverage has Nasdaq-100 down over 2%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The giveback is holding rather than deepening further, but the Nasdaq is still giving back about a third of Monday's historic gain before the open.

headlines.headline: Nvidia -6% premarket to about $155, after soaring 31% on Monday and adding more than $900B in market value. Despite Monday's surge, the stock enters the day still down more than 30% from its Oct 6 record closing high.
headlines.why_it_matters: The re-pricing of the governance overhang continues even after the record one-day gain — the market is weighing the unresolved investigations (SEC probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Dec 1 House testimony) more than the leadership return.

headlines.headline: Chips and memory broadly lower premarket: Micron, SK Hynix, Intel and Marvell all down more than 6%; AMD and Broadcom down roughly 5%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) and Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) each dropped more than 5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff is sector-wide across semis and memory, not just Nvidia — Monday's rally is being unwound across the whole AI hardware complex.

headlines.headline: Sanofi agreed to acquire US drugmaker Insmed for $41 billion. Insmed shares +15% premarket; Sanofi's US-traded stock +7%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning's biggest deal news is a defensive-sector counterweight to the tech selloff — M&A appetite is alive even on a down tape.

headlines.headline: HPE now -12% premarket despite better-than-expected results and raised guidance; Dell -7% ahead of its Q3 results after the close (analysts expect EPS $6.61 on revenue $49.24B). Semtech -12% premarket after its beat. Analog Devices -10.2% premarket despite strong results (single-source social recap).
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat-and-fall pattern is deepening — the bar is the guide and demand durability, not the quarter. The Analog Devices figure is single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile. Dell is the next check on AI server demand after HPE's guide-driven selloff.

headlines.headline: Dick's Sporting Goods +16.7% premarket after earning $1.94/share vs $1.40 expected and raising full-year guidance — a beat by a wide margin.
headlines.why_it_matters: Another beat-and-raise being bought on a down tape — consumer spending is holding up, and the market is rewarding guide quality, sharpening the contrast with the chip selloffs.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) -6% premarket, trading just below the $83 level it priced its record-setting IPO at last week. Alphabet (GOOGL) -1% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade's newest public name is now under water vs its IPO price within a week — sentiment is cooling across the whole AI complex, not just hardware.

headlines.headline: Alibaba's New York-listed depositary receipts fell premarket after one of its subsidiaries was added to a US blacklist intended to curb its access to American chips.
headlines.why_it_matters: A fresh US-China chip-access restriction landing on a day the chip complex is already selling off — it adds a policy layer to the AI-trade unwind.

headlines.headline: US rate futures price a 97.6% probability of a 25bp hike (2.4% for 50bp) at the December FOMC meeting, per Barchart — a touch softer than the 100% hike likelihood carried in the 5 AM brief.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hike pricing is near-certain but not absolute — today's consumer confidence and FOMC minutes are the next inputs before Wednesday's PCE/GDP dump and the Dec 9 meeting.
